main_text.l: Alium mundum esse præter hunc qui sit in-genitus, Perata.
Materiam mundi Deo coæternam esse, Se-leuciani, Hermiani, Procliani, Hermogeniani.
Ex sudore & metu Æonum factum esse mun-dum, Valentiniani, Secundiani.
Principia hæc tria esse increata nimirum, a-quam, ignem & tenebras, Audiani.
Mundi huius statum esse æternum, Eter-nales.
Angelos esse ex Dei sapientia velut matre, propagatione natos, Basilidiani, Gnostici, Ar-chontici.
Ex concupiscentia tenebrarum & impetu in lucem, Nicolaitæ.
Angelos barbaris nominibus & magicis ap-pellant Nicolaitæ, Gnostici, Seueriani.
Angelos præfici cælis, quenque suo orbi, Ba-silidiani.
Bonos Angelos revera cum mulieribus co-ire ad homines procreandos, Sethiani.
Diabolum esse natum ex tricesimo Æone, Valentiniani, Archontici.
Cælos esse alios ex aliis fluentes, & numero 365. Basilidiani.
Stellas & astra esse prædita ratione, Priscil-

page.notes: Marginal reference marks (ornaments and letters such as "o", "ɑ") sit beside several lines and were not transcribed as notes; they are typographic reference signs for the sects named in italics and are shown here as printed where legible. The page is heavily spotted; words near the stains (e.g. "ex sudore", "Valentiniani") are read with some doubt. The word-initial letters in the italic sect names (e.g. "Basilidiani", "Gnostici") are partly obscured by ink spread; the forms given follow the printed text as far as legible. The bottom line breaks mid-word ("Priscil-") and continues on the next page. Headings are set in roman type larger than the text; I have used level 2 as they are subordinate to the chapter-level heading of this work. The Greek-looking marks in the margin were not legible enough to transcribe.
